bull.b: TSMC’s high advanced-node mix demonstrates strong technology leadership and customer adoption in the most valuable parts of the foundry market. This supports pricing power, scale benefits, and durable relevance as AI and high-performance computing demand increasingly require leading-edge manufacturing.

Low and improving leverage gives TSMC substantial financial flexibility to fund fabs, advanced packaging, and technology development without relying excessively on new borrowing. Rising equity and approximately 41.2% TTM ROE also indicate that expansion is being supported by strong underlying earnings power.

The combination of a strong growth outlook and planned N2 capacity expansion positions TSMC to convert sustained AI and high-performance-computing demand into longer-term revenue. A progressing A14 roadmap and broader capacity buildout further reinforce the company’s strategic manufacturing advantage.

bear.b: The 2 nm ramp and overseas fab expansion can weigh on profitability before new facilities reach efficient utilization. Expected dilution of 3%-4% over the coming years creates a lasting execution risk, potentially limiting margin expansion even while leading-edge demand remains strong.

TSMC generates strong operating cash flow, but its large fab and technology investments absorb a significant portion of earnings. Lower free-cash-flow conversion can make cash generation more variable through the cycle and constrain flexibility if demand or utilization weakens during the expansion program.

Although AI demand is exceptionally strong, exposure to consumer and other price-sensitive markets leaves TSMC vulnerable to semiconductor cycles and customer spending decisions. Weaker affordability or macroeconomic conditions could reduce utilization and create volatility outside the current high-growth areas.
